boards.title: Your First Weekend at South Dakota State University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A campus-first, under-21-safe sequence that mixes orientation, recreation, local culture, and a meal stop.

cards.title: Start at the campus symbol
cards.subtitle: Friday arrival • Coughlin Campanile
cards.notes: Begin your walk at the 165-foot chimes tower, then use the surrounding paths to orient yourself before heading to nearby campus services.
cards.short_summary: A recognizable first landmark for getting your bearings.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU describes Coughlin Campanile as a 165-foot chimes tower and the face of the university; it plays music between classes.
cards.source_title: Coughlin Campanile building | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: The building page says visitors wishing to climb the 180 steps should check out a key at the Alumni Center or University Police Department.

cards.title: Make the Union your first indoor stop
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • University Student Union
cards.notes: Pause at the Student Union to locate dining, Student Activities, Student Connection and Engagement, and the campus bookstore in one building.
cards.short_summary: A central place to connect campus services with your weekend plan.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU identifies the University Student Union as the heart of campus life and lists Student Activities, dining, student services, and Jackrabbit Central there.
cards.source_title: University Student Union | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Academic-year hours listed by SDSU are 7 a.m.–11 p.m. Monday–Friday, 8 a.m.–11 p.m. Saturday, and 10 a.m.–11 p.m. Sunday; breaks and holidays differ.

cards.title: Settle in with a campus study stop
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon • Hilton M. Briggs Library
cards.notes: Walk through the three levels to identify study rooms, computers, printing, and the collections you may want once classes begin.
cards.short_summary: A practical first look at SDSU’s academic workspaces.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU says Hilton M. Briggs Library has three floors of academic materials, study space, computers, printers, scanners, and bookable study rooms.
cards.source_title: Hilton M. Briggs Library building | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Confirm library access and hours before visiting, especially during breaks or holidays.

cards.title: Try a recreation option before dinner
cards.subtitle: Friday evening • Miller Wellness Center
cards.notes: Use the recreation and fitness facilities for a low-key activity, and check the current schedule if you want the pool, climbing wall, or esports lounge.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation stop with several activity choices.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU says the Miller Wellness Center houses fitness equipment, recreational and intramural programs, wellness education, health services, and counseling services.
cards.source_title: University Wellbeing | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: SDSU’s posted fall/spring facility hours include service until 11 p.m. Monday–Thursday and 10 p.m. Friday and Sunday; schedules vary for breaks, holidays, and events.

cards.title: Add a Dairy Bar treat
cards.subtitle: Friday evening • SDSU Dairy Bar
cards.notes: Choose ice cream, milk, coffee, or a snack, then watch production through the large windows while you take a break from the first-day walk.
cards.short_summary: A campus food stop tied to SDSU dairy production.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU states that the Dairy Bar serves ice cream, milk, coffee, and snacks, with seating and windows overlooking production.
cards.source_title: Dairy Bar building | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: SDSU lists Dairy Bar hours as Monday–Friday, 8:30 a.m.–5:30 p.m.; verify hours before making it an evening stop.

cards.title: Spend Saturday morning with the galleries
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning • South Dakota Art Museum
cards.notes: Make a gallery loop and look for works from the museum’s South Dakota-connected collections; allow time for changing exhibitions rather than a fixed route.
cards.short_summary: A free museum visit on the west side of campus.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU says the South Dakota Art Museum displays work by Ada Caldwell, Harvey Dunn, Oscar Howe, and others, and that admission is free.
cards.source_title: South Dakota Art Museum building | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: SDSU notes that exhibits change every few months; check the museum’s current visitor information before arrival.

cards.title: Follow with agricultural history
cards.subtitle: Saturday midday • South Dakota Agricultural Heritage Museum
cards.notes: Browse the permanent objects and displays, then use the exhibits as a prompt for learning how agriculture and rural life shaped the state.
cards.short_summary: An official state museum located on the SDSU campus.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU identifies the South Dakota Agricultural Heritage Museum as the official state museum that collects, preserves, and interprets South Dakota agricultural and rural-life history.
cards.source_title: About the Agricultural Heritage Museum | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: SDSU lists hours as 10 a.m.–5 p.m. Monday–Saturday and 1–5 p.m. Sunday, with Sunday closures January–March.

cards.title: Walk the public arboretum trails
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon • McCrory Gardens
cards.notes: Take the accessible public arboretum trails for an outdoor reset, and save the formal gardens for a time when you have valid SDSU ID or paid admission.
cards.short_summary: A free public trail walk beside SDSU’s gardens.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU states that McCrory Gardens’ arboretum has about 1.6 miles of public-accessible trails open from dawn to dusk and free to explore.
cards.source_title: Plan Your Visit to McCrory | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: The arboretum trails are free and open dawn to dusk. Formal-garden hours and admission vary seasonally; SDSU students receive free entry with valid SDSU ID.

cards.title: Check the arena calendar for a game
cards.subtitle: Saturday evening • First Bank & Trust Arena
cards.notes: If the public event calendar has a suitable game or match, attend it; otherwise, walk by the renovated arena and save a ticketed event for another weekend.
cards.short_summary: The current home venue for Jackrabbit basketball, volleyball, and wrestling.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU says First Bank & Trust Arena opened in fall 2024 and serves as the home competition venue for Jackrabbit basketball, volleyball, and wrestling.
cards.source_title: First Bank & Trust Arena building | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: Event availability and admission vary; use the official athletics or arena calendar before planning an entry.

cards.title: Close with an outdoor landmark walk
cards.subtitle: Sunday afternoon • Coolidge Sylvan Theatre
cards.notes: Visit the outdoor theatre and its hand-forged gates, then look for public plays, concerts, or celebrations scheduled there later in the semester.
cards.short_summary: A historic outdoor stage still used for campus occasions.
cards.evidence_claim: SDSU says Coolidge Sylvan Theatre was dedicated in 1927, retains hand-forged gates, and is still used for plays, inaugurations, and outdoor celebrations.
cards.source_title: Coolidge Sylvan Theatre building | South Dakota State University
cards.access_notes: This is an outdoor landmark; check the university event calendar for public performances or celebrations.
